title: 2024年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
paperTitle: 2024年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
passage:
P1 Some people have said aging is more a slide into forgetfulness than a journey towards wisdom. However, a growing body of research suggests that late-in-life learning is possible. In reality, education does an aging brain good.

P2 Throughout life, people's brains constantly renovate themselves. In the late 1960s, British brain scientist Geoffrey Raisman spied growth in damaged brain regions of rats through an electron microscope; their brains were forging new connections. This meant brains may change every time a person learns something new.

P3 Of course, that doesn't mean the brain isn't affected by the effects of time. Just as height usually declines over the years, so does brain volume: Humans lose about 4 percent every decade starting in their 40s. But that reduction doesn't necessarily make people think slower; as long as we are alive and functioning, we can alter our brains with new information and experiences.

P4 In fact, scientists now suspect accumulating novel experiences, facts, and skills can keep people's minds more flexible. New pathways can strengthen our ever-changing mental structure, even as the brain shrinks.

P5 Conventional fixes like word puzzles and brain-training apps can contribute to mental durability. Even something as simple as taking a different route to the grocery store or going somewhere new on vacation can keep the brain healthy.

P6 A desire for new life challenges can further boost brainpower. Research about aging adults who take on new enterprises shows improved function and memory as well as a reduced risk of mental disease. Openness—a characteristic defined by curiosity and a desire for knowledge—may also help folks pass brain tests. Some folks are born with this take-in-the-world attitude, but those who aren't as genetically gifted aren't necessarily out of luck. While genes can encourage an interest in doing new things, a 2012 study in the journal Psychology and Aging found completing reasoning tasks like puzzles and number games can enhance that desire for novel experiences, which can, in turn, refresh the brain. That's why brain scientist Richard Kennedy says "It's not that old dogs can't learn new tricks. It's that maybe old dogs don't realize why they should."

questions.q: What do some people think of aging adults?
options: Their wisdom grows as time goes by.
Their memory gradually deteriorates.
They can benefit from late-in-life learning.
They are likely to have mental health issues.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do some people think of aging adults? 用 what do ... think of 直接问看法，且明 确限定主语 some people，属于对原文具体观点的事实复述。

【拆句】Q51 主干为 What do some people think of aging adults，think of 表示「对……的看 法」，think 与 of 分立但语义绑定，基础薄弱考生易把 think of 拆开理解为「想到」，注 意它是「评价」之义。

【定位】Some people have said aging is more a slide into forgetfulness than a journey towards wisdom. 某些人说，衰老与其说是一段通向智慧的旅程，不如说是一步步滑向健忘。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 题干问 some people 的看法，原文 some people 恰恰用 more A than B 否定了「通 向智慧」这一端，Their wisdom grows as time goes by. 正好与之相反。 B) ✓ 正确 a slide into forgetfulness ↔memory gradually deteriorates 预判「记性变差」与 Their memory gradually deteriorates. 的语义完全一致，且整句 都被原文 slide into forgetfulness 覆盖，无添加成分。 C) 张冠李戴 They can benefit from late-in-life learning. 是作者及研究方的观点（a growing body of research suggests that late-in-life learning is possible），不属于题干所问 的 some people。 D) 无中生有 首段并未提及 some people 认为衰老会导致 mental health issues（精神健康问 题），原文只说「健忘」（forgetfulness），健忘不等于心理疾病。 我们能从Geoffrey Raisman的发现中得出什么结论? A) 大脑损伤严重阻碍人的学习。 B) 脑力衰退的速度比我们想象的要慢。 C) 大脑可以通过学习得到更新和改善。 D) 大脑在新条件下建立连接。

questions.q: What can we conclude from Geoffrey Raisman's finding?
options: Brain damage seriously hinders one's learning.
Brain power weakens slower than we imagine.
Brains can refresh and improve with learning.
Brains forge connections under new conditions.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we conclude from Geoffrey Raisman's finding? 出现 conclude，要求从已述 事实再推一步得出结论。 52. What can we conclude from Geoffrey Raisman's finding? A) Brain damage seriously hinders one's learning. B) Brain power weakens slower than we imagine. C) Brains can refresh and improve with learning. D) Brains forge connections under new conditions.

【拆句】Q52 句中 what 是 conclude 的宾语，from Geoffrey Raisman's finding 是状语，结构平 铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】In the late 1960s, British brain scientist Geoffrey Raisman spied growth in damaged brain regions of rats through an electron microscope; their brains were forging new connections. This meant brains may change every time a person learns something new. 上世纪 60 年代末，英国脑科学家 Geoffrey Raisman 用电子显微镜观察到老鼠受损脑区长 出新生组织；它们的大脑正在缔结新连接。这意味着，每当一个人学到新东西，大脑都可能 发生改变。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文只说 Raisman 在「受损脑区」观察到新连接，并未谈论 brain damage 对 learning 的影响，更没有 hinders 这种负向判断。 B) 无中生有 原文未做「比想象慢/快」的速度比较，brain power weakens slower 这种比较关系在 Raisman 段并不存在。 C) ✓ 正确 brains may change every time a person learns something new ↔ Brains can refresh and improve with learning. 预判核心是「学习—大脑改变/更新」，Brains can refresh and improve with learning. 用 refresh、improve 概括 change + forging new connections 的双层含 义，且 with learning 直接对应「每当学新东西」，整句无溢出。 D) 答非所问 Brains forge connections under new conditions. 几乎照搬 their brains were forging new connections，但题干问的是 conclude（结论意义），而该选项只重复了 实验事实，没把意义说出来。 即使大脑萎缩,有什么能帮助维持大脑健康? A) 用传统方式进行日常事务。 B) 避免担心我们的心智持久性。 C) 模仿老狗学新把戏的方式。 D) 用新颖的方式处理日常任务。

questions.q: What is one thing that helps maintain the health of our brain even as it shrinks?
options: Doing daily routines by conventional means.
Avoiding worrying about our mental durability.
Imitating old dogs' way of learning new tricks.
Approaching everyday tasks in novel ways.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is one thing that helps maintain the health of our brain 用 one thing that ... 直 接问一件具体做法，属事实复述。 53. What is one thing that helps maintain the health of our brain even as it shrinks? A) Doing daily routines by conventional means. B) Avoiding worrying about our mental durability. C) Imitating old dogs' way of learning new tricks. D) Approaching everyday tasks in novel ways.

【拆句】Q53 主干 What is one thing，其后 that ... 是定语从句修饰 thing；even as it shrinks 是让步状语，as 此处等于 although，it 指代 brain，须留意 it 的指代关系不要错认 成 health。

【定位】Even something as simple as taking a different route to the grocery store or going somewhere new on vacation can keep the brain healthy. 哪怕是像换条路去超市、或换个地方度假这样简单的事，也能让大脑保持健康。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文强调要「换新方式」做日常事，而 Doing daily routines by conventional means. 强调用 conventional means（常规方式），方向完全相反。 B) 无中生有 Avoiding worrying about our mental durability. 提到「避免担忧脑力耐久度」，但原 文 P5 谈的是「具体做法」，从未谈论「担忧」或「避免担忧」这个心理层面。 C) 偷换概念 原文末段 It\'s not that old dogs can\'t learn new tricks. It\'s that maybe old dogs don\'t realize why they should. 中的 old dogs 是比喻人，不是真的「狗的学习方 式」；Imitating old dogs\' way of learning new tricks. 把比喻当字面，且并非 P5 的 护脑手段。 D) ✓ 正确 taking a different route to the grocery store or going somewhere new on vacation ↔ Approaching everyday tasks in novel ways. 预判的两个关键语义点「日常事」和「新方式」在 Approaching everyday tasks in novel ways. 中一一对应，没有任何额外成分。 作者认为什么有助于改善大脑功能? A) 保持好奇心和求知欲。 B) 渴望在年老时通过大脑测试。 C) 迎接生活挑战并避免风险。 D) 增强对严重精神疾病的免疫力。

questions.q: What does the author say can contribute to the improvement of brain function?
options: Being curious and desiring knowledge.
Being eager to pass brain tests at an old age.
Rising to life's challenges and avoiding risks.
Boosting immunity to serious mental diseases.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say can contribute to the improvement of brain function? 直 接问 author 提出的「促进项」，是对原文表述的事实复述。

【拆句】Q54 主干为 What does the author say can contribute to ...，what 既作 say 的宾语，又 作 can contribute to 的逻辑主语（省略关系代词的嵌套从句结构），基础薄弱考生易在两 个谓语间断错语义，建议拆为「作者说，[什么]能促进脑功能提升」。 54. What does the author say can contribute to the improvement of brain function? A) Being curious and desiring knowledge. B) Being eager to pass brain tests at an old age. C) Rising to life's challenges and avoiding risks. D) Boosting immunity to serious mental diseases.

【定位】Openness—a characteristic defined by curiosity and a desire for knowledge—may also help folks pass brain tests. 「开放性」——一种由好奇心和求知欲所定义的特质——也可以帮助人们顺利通过脑力 测试。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 curiosity and a desire for knowledge ↔Being curious and desiring knowledge. 预判的两个核心要素「好奇心」和「求知欲」在 Being curious and desiring knowledge. 中由同根词分别承接，且选项整体只表达这两点，无多余成分，无遗漏。 B) 偷换概念 原文说 openness 能帮助 pass brain tests，是「特质 → 通过测试」的因果；Being eager to pass brain tests at an old age. 把「通过测试」偷换成「渴望通过测试」， 把结果偷换成动机，方向不同。 C) 无中生有 原文 A desire for new life challenges can further boost brainpower. 只说「迎接新 挑战」能提升脑力，从未提到 avoiding risks（规避风险）；C 项硬加了「规避风险」 这一成分。 D) 偷换概念 原文 improved function and memory as well as a reduced risk of mental disease 中，reduced risk of mental disease 是 take on new enterprises 带来的「结果之 一」，而非「促进脑功能的手段」；Boosting immunity to serious mental diseases. 把这一结果倒置成促进手段。 2012年《心理学与衰老》期刊研究的发现是什么? A) 想要解决谜题能增强人的推理能力。 B) 玩数字游戏会意外刺激人的记忆力。 C) 渴望新体验有助于更新大脑。 D) 学习新把戏不应该只限于老狗。

questions.q: What is the finding of the 2012 study in the journal Psychology and Aging?
options: Wishing to solve puzzles enhances one's reasoning power.
Playing number games unexpectedly stimulates one's memory.
Desiring new experiences can help to renovate the brain.
Learning new tricks should not be confined to old dogs only.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the finding of the 2012 study 直接问研究发现内容，属定位+复述型问法。

【拆句】Q55 主干为 What is the finding，of the 2012 study 与 in the journal Psychology and Aging 都是修饰 finding 的介词短语，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 55. What is the finding of the 2012 study in the journal Psychology and Aging? A) Wishing to solve puzzles enhances one's reasoning power. B) Playing number games unexpectedly stimulates one's memory. C) Desiring new experiences can help to renovate the brain. D) Learning new tricks should not be confined to old dogs only.

【定位】While genes can encourage an interest in doing new things, a 2012 study in the journal Psychology and Aging found completing reasoning tasks like puzzles and number games can enhance that desire for novel experiences, which can, in turn, refresh the brain. 尽管基因能在一定程度上鼓励一个人对新事物的兴趣，但 2012 年发表在《Psychology and Aging》期刊上的一项研究发现，完成像谜题、数字游戏这样的推理任务能够强化「想 要新体验」的欲望，而这种欲望反过来又能刷新大脑。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文是「做推理任务（含 puzzles）→ 强化对新体验的欲望 → 刷新大脑」，Wishing to solve puzzles enhances one\'s reasoning power. 反过来变成「想做谜题 → 提升 推理力」，方向被颠倒，且原文从未谈 enhance reasoning power。 B) 无中生有 原文链条终点是 refresh the brain（刷新大脑），不是 stimulates one\'s memory （刺激记忆）；且 unexpectedly（出乎意料地）也不在原文里。 C) ✓ 正确 that desire for novel experiences, which can, in turn, refresh the brain ↔ Desiring new experiences can help to renovate the brain. 预判的落脚点「对新体验的欲望能刷新大脑」与 Desiring new experiences can help to renovate the brain. 在主语、动作、对象上一一对位，无添加成分。 D) 张冠李戴 Learning new tricks should not be confined to old dogs only. 改写自结尾的 Richard Kennedy 引语，是 brain scientist Kennedy 的比喻金句，而非 2012 年那项 研究的 finding。
